mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Megane 1.5 dCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a Renault Megane 1.5 dCi typically costs £500-£3,461 for the supply-only unit. Fitting adds 8-12 hours of labour at £65-£90/hr, bringing the total fitted cost to £1,500-£3,500 at an independent specialist. Dealer pricing is significantly higher.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Renault Megane 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are hard starting (especially when cold), unstable idle, loss of power, injection fault warnings, and white smoke from the exhaust. Fault codes such as P0470 are common. On early K9K models (pre-2011), injector failure is often caused by metal swarf from a failing high-pressure fuel pump.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Megane 1.5 dCi a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 dCi has a double personality - some units exceed 300,000 km without issue, while others suffer serious failures. Pre-2011 models are more prone to injector and fuel system issues, while post-2011 models are significantly more robust. Regular maintenance - particularly timing belt replacement - is the key to longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Megane 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value. Megane II examples are worth £500-£2,000 - a full engine replacement at £1,800-£2,800 may exceed the car's value. Megane III examples (£1,000-£5,000) may justify replacement if the rest of the car is in good condition. Megane IV examples with higher values (£4,000-£12,000) generally justify replacement.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the K9K 636 and K9K 656 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The K9K 636 produces 110PS (81kW) and was fitted to Megane III models from 2008-2016. The K9K 656 produces 90PS (66kW) and was fitted to Megane III and IV models from 2009-2019. Both share the same 1.5-litre (1,461cc) displacement and the same K9K architecture.

mainEntity.name: Does the Renault Megane 1.5 dCi have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 dCi (K9K) uses a timing belt, not a chain. The belt requires replacement at the manufacturer-recommended interval - typically every 72,000 miles or 5 years, whichever comes first. Neglecting the timing belt can lead to catastrophic engine failure if it breaks.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Megane 1.5 dCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Megane 1.5 dCi, powered by the legendary K9K engine, has been a mainstay of the Megane range since the early 2000s. First introduced in the Clio in 2001, this 1.5-litre turbo diesel became one of Europe's most popular small-capacity diesel engines, fitted to Megane II, III and IV generations. The K9K engine has a cast-iron block, an aluminium cylinder head and a timing belt drive, and its widespread use across multiple manufacturers (including Nissan, Mercedes and Dacia) has made it a familiar unit to UK specialists.

milestones.description: 2009 (Megane II) - Early K9K engines introduced (65PS-105PS); Bosch and Delphi fuel systems; Euro 3 and Euro 4 emissions
2016 (Megane III) - K9K 636, K9K 646, K9K 656, K9K 836, K9K 837, K9K 846 variants; 86PS-110PS outputs; Euro 5 compliance; DPF fitted on many variants
2011 - Timing belt failures reported on some K9K units; revised components introduced
present (Megane IV) - K9K 646, K9K 656, K9K 657, K9K 872 and other variants; 90PS-115PS outputs; Euro 6 compliance; AdBlue/SCR systems on Blue dCi variants
present - K9K continues in production with ongoing emissions updates

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Renault Megane 1.5 dCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Renault Megane 1.5 dCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Megane 1.5 dCi (K9K family) is one of Europe's most popular diesel engines, but it has several well-documented failure points. Some K9K units exceed 300,000 km without issue, while others suffer serious failures. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Fuel System Issues in the Renault Megane 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Megane 1.5 dCi (K9K, particularly pre-2011 models)
problems.rootCause: Injectors are prone to wear over time, causing hard starting (especially when cold), unstable idle, loss of power and "injection fault" warnings. On early K9K engines, the high-pressure fuel pump can wear prematurely, producing metal swarf that contaminates the entire fuel system. Fault codes such as P0470 or "injection failure" messages are common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New injectors, fuel system flush, new fuel filter
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before pump swarf has contaminated the entire system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if pump failure has caused widespread fuel system contamination or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework to your Renault Megane 1.5 dCi. Megane II examples typically range £500-£2,000; Megane III examples range £1,000-£5,000; Megane IV examples range £4,000-£12,000. - Vehicle worth under ~£2,000: used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit - or consider scrapping if repair costs exceed value - Vehicle worth ~£2,000-£5,000: evaluate both; injector replacement is viable if the car is otherwise sound - Vehicle worth £5,000+: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability
problems.recommendation: If your Megane 1.5 dCi has rough running, hard starting or loss of power, have the injectors and fuel pump inspected immediately. Early injector replacement costs £500-£900 at a specialist. Ignoring the issue risks widespread fuel system contamination and a £1,800-£2,800 engine replacement bill.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Renault Megane 1.5 dCi engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - The K9K's Critical Service Item
problems.rootCause: The K9K uses a timing belt, not a chain. Renault recommends replacement every 5 years, with some sources suggesting 72,000 miles. Some 2009-2011 models suffered from premature belt wear. If the belt breaks, the engine suffers catastrophic valve-to-piston contact, requiring a full rebuild or replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing belt, tensioner, water pump
repairOptions.longevity: Essential preventative maintenance every 72,000 miles or 5 years

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has broken and caused valve/piston damage

problems.recommendation: Timing belt replacement is the single most important maintenance item on the Megane 1.5 dCi. If your car is approaching 72,000 miles or is over 5 years old, have the belt replaced immediately. A £300-£500 preventative job is far cheaper than a £1,800-£2,800 engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare Renault Megane 1.5 dCi engine replacement costs

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - Boost and Power Loss in the Renault Megane 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Megane 1.5 dCi (K9K, particularly higher-mileage examples)
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger failure on the 1.5 dCi can manifest as a loud whine, clouds of smoke, loss of oil or total loss of power. Common fault codes include P0299 (turbo underboost) and P2263 (turbo performance issue). Stuck turbo actuators, split pipes, and MAF sensor issues are also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned turbocharger unit, oil feed pipe replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo failure has caused debris to enter the engine oil system

problems.recommendation: If your Megane 1.5 dCi has lost power, is smoking or making unusual noises, have the turbocharger inspected immediately. Early turbo replacement costs £500-£1,000 at a specialist. Ignoring the issue can lead to catastrophic engine failure as debris from a failed turbo can destroy the bottom end.
